name: Role 2 Field Hospital in Heat
location_context: Deployed Role 2 medical facility, hot arid climate, summer. Intermittent host-nation supply and a road resupply route that is open daily. SYNTHETIC scenario, not a real location.

grid_availability.note: SYNTHETIC. Host-nation supply is present for roughly twelve hours in each twenty-four, and absent through the hottest part of the afternoon.

weather_profile.description: Hot arid summer, clear skies, large diurnal swing (SYNTHETIC)

mobility_requirement.note: The facility is not required to relocate during this mission.

operator_priorities.statement: The cold chain must never be interrupted; blood products are irreplaceable here.
The operating theatre and its environmental control must be available whenever surgery is scheduled.
Casualty regulation and the telemedicine link must remain available.
Keep the wards cool; a warmer setpoint is clinically acceptable for a period if it protects theatre and cold chain.
Run sterilisation on its schedule if the cooling load allows it.
Minimise the number of single points of failure: this facility cannot be evacuated quickly.

notes: MM-DEMO-003 is an invented scenario written to test whether the MissionSpec generalises beyond a fuel-limited mission (RQ-001). It does not reflect any armed forces requirement, doctrine, or real deployment.
The binding constraint here is heat, not fuel. Fuel is ample by design (2600 L with a daily resupply route assumed open) so that the trade-offs the planner has to make are thermal ones.
Cooling demand is temperature-dependent and the ambient swings from 26 to 44 degC, so the load the node must serve at 1500 is roughly twice what it serves at 0500.
The leading operator objective is not fuel but single points of failure: a facility that cannot be evacuated quickly would rather carry redundancy than save litres.
No adversary behaviour is modelled. Disruption is represented only as asset unavailability.
